clue.text: Wager involving question put to everyone after British game

indicators.note: the clue places everyone after British, so that piece follows it
a bet involving something holds it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a wager is a bet
to question is to ask
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A gambler asks a whole group about a bet on a British sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' and 'after' are the two placing words; 'put to' is only a link joining question and everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Basketball is an example of a game, played with hoops and a large ball.

clue.text: Allure of Scottish isle, reportedly last for ferry

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the island's name is to be taken as it is spoken

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde, off western Scotland

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word ferry

explanation.surface: A tourist admires a Scottish island and hears it is the final stop for the ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTE, an island off western Scotland, said out loud sounds like BEAUT; the last letter of 'ferry' adds Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure and attractiveness are near synonyms: both describe the quality of being pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Piazza is level

definitions.meaning: a piazza is an open public plaza in a town, especially in Italy
level in the sense of even, with neither side owing

explanation.surface: A short remark that an Italian plaza is flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A town square is an open plaza; being square means being even or level, as in a contest.

clue.text: European guys learn this foreign language?

indicators.note: foreign means strange or out of place, so these letters are rearranged into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: European men are learning a language from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges GUYS LEARN THIS; the question mark admits that this accent from south-east England is hardly a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Estuary English is a variety of speech from around the Thames estuary, a loose sense of a language.

clue.text: Last drink? Here's to you!

parts.note: the bottom of a league table or list is last place
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Raising a final glass with a toast to a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last drink?' reads like a call at closing time but supplies both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a cheery drinking toast, a call to drain the glass, much like here's to you.

clue.text: Beautiful stone — there's one in US plaza I'll fancy

indicators.note: the word in tells us the single piece is placed within the rearranged letters
to fancy is to imagine or invent, so these letters are made into something new

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a lovely gemstone set in an American plaza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges US PLAZA I'LL, and 'in' slips I (one) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapis lazuli is a deep blue semi-precious rock prized for jewellery and ornament.

clue.text: Hit low, mostly, and hard

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: a bass note or voice is low in pitch
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A boxer lands a hard punch below the belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BASS to BAS. 'Hit low' looks like a foul blow, but 'low' is the musical word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bash someone is to strike them hard, a forceful hit.

clue.text: Impenetrable in appearance, even

parts.note: an air is a look or manner, as in an air of confidence
a tight contest is a close, even one

explanation.surface: Something looks impossible to break into, even on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed container lets nothing through, so it is impenetrable to gas, and figuratively an unassailable case.

clue.text: No blokes do

parts.note: a do is a party; one where men are barred is the women-only celebration before a wedding

explanation.surface: Reads like a flat statement that men never do something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a verb but is the noun for a party; blokes is British slang for men.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the celebration a bride-to-be holds with female friends only, a party with no men.

clue.text: Promising band put on prior to match

definitions.text: Promising band put on prior to match

parts.words: Promising band put on prior to match
parts.note: a band marking a promise to marry is worn before the match, meaning the wedding

explanation.surface: A musical group showing promise is booked before a sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians and 'match' a game, but here a match is a marriage and the band is worn on the finger.
explanation.definitionFit: This ring is given when a couple promise to marry, so it is worn before the wedding.

clue.text: Ardour lit? Oddly, being mature

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions, the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Wondering whether lit-up passion is a sign of being grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' takes letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of ARDOUR LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fully grown, past adolescence, is mature, synonymous here as adjectives.

clue.text: Type of cricket clue, along with last

parts.note: a tip is a hint or clue
and means along with
to last is to run on or continue, as a play may run for months

explanation.surface: A crossword setter describes a cricket clue, plus a final one.
explanation.walkthrough: TIP AND RUN is an informal cricket game where the batter must run every time the ball is hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip and run is a casual variety of the bat-and-ball game where every hit forces a dash between wickets.

clue.text: Rat on criminal, cheat and twister

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or cheat them

explanation.surface: An informer betrays a crook, a swindler and a trickster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges RAT ON into TORNA. 'twister' looks like another villain but is the storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Twister is an informal name for a whirling windstorm, the funnel-shaped kind.

clue.text: Endurance of man? It's beaten by females at the centre

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are beaten, whisked up, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: the contraction gives its three letters with the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: at the centre takes the middle letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man's staying power is outdone by women in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' mixes MAN and ITS into STAMIN; 'at the centre' gives A, the fourth of seven letters in 'females'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the ability to keep going under strain, which is endurance.

clue.text: Film somehow suited — see why?

indicators.note: somehow means in some unexplained way, so the letters end up in an unstated order

explanation.surface: Someone finds a film somehow suits them and asks why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges SUITED and SEE WHY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes Wide Shut is Stanley Kubrick's last movie, from 1999, starring Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman.

clue.text: Obstruct opening of inn, rent-free building

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
building means putting together, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: Someone blocks plans for an inn housed in a building with no rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening of' gives I; 'building' rearranges RENT-FREE. 'building' looks like a noun but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere is to get in the way, hindering or meddling, so it can mean obstruct.

clue.text: Identifying a politician falling into police trap

indicators.note: falling into the trap places these pieces inside the other word

parts.note: a sting is an undercover operation set up to catch criminals
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is caught in a police operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling into' signals the container; 'Identifying' is a verb form, matching the -ING answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamping a document marks it with an official sign, labelling and identifying it.

clue.text: Bureaucrat from Iran, possibly supporting Morocco's leader also

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that supports another sits below it
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: and means also, in addition

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: An official from Iran perhaps backs a Moroccan ruler too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IRAN into ARIN, which 'supporting' places beneath M and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a senior civil servant, a powerful official, after the term for imperial Chinese officials.

clue.text: Railway buff returned pictures in protest after changes made

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for pictures is read the other way

parts.note: pictures as paintings are art

indicators.note: once changes have been made, the word's letters stand in a new order

explanation.surface: Artwork is sent back amid a protest once alterations are made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives TRA; 'after changes made' rearranges the seven letters of 'protest'. A trainspotter is the British term for a railway enthusiast logging engine numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter collects sightings of locomotives, the classic railway enthusiast.

clue.text: See 5
Let on about meat

parts.note: re means about or concerning
veal is the meat of calves

explanation.surface: Someone gives away a secret concerning meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let on' looks like letting something happen but means to disclose.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to disclose a secret, so it means to make it known.

clue.text: Note what Anglicanism has to offer?

definitions.meaning: a note in the scale, the one near the centre of a piano keyboard
the eleven-letter word has one central letter, a C, at its heart

explanation.surface: Asking what the Church of England has to give.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the sixth of the eleven letters in 'Anglicanism' is C. It also suggests the moderate middle way of the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle C is the musical note near the centre of the piano keys.

clue.text: Soldier chasing my dog

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier runs after the speaker's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' looks possessive but is an exclamation of surprise; 'chasing' sets the soldier second.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Struggle to survive in desert heat, perhaps

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side
a heat is an example of a race, a qualifying round

explanation.surface: Fighting to stay alive in scorching desert temperatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like sand dunes but is a verb, and 'heat' is a qualifying round, not the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the relentless competitive grind of working life, a constant scramble to get by.

clue.text: On hand, popular book

parts.note: something in is fashionable or popular
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A popular book kept close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in reserve is kept available for use, ready if needed.

clue.text: Busy female leaving brew

indicators.note: a letter leaving a word is removed from it

parts.note: to brew tea is to infuse it

explanation.surface: A woman is too busy and walks out on her tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes F from INFUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line or room that is occupied is busy, taken by someone at that moment.

clue.text: Medal from Pentagon, gold

indicators.note: from tells us some letters are taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for gold

explanation.surface: A gold decoration awarded by the US military headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the last three letters of 'Pentagon'. GONG is British slang for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British informal slang for a medal or decoration, especially an honour.

clue.text: Cross, girl led astray making meal

parts.note: to cross breeds is to mix them

indicators.note: astray means off course, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry girl is misled while cooking dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but means mix; 'astray' rearranges GIRL LED into EDGRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed grill is a dish of assorted grilled meats such as sausage, bacon and chops, a hearty plateful.
